commitments.text: POST /offline-reports accepts a JSON body with description:string, species:string, optional temperature:number, and a client-generated report_id (UUID v4) as idempotency key. Returns 201 with report_id and creation_timestamp.
commitments.rationale: Offline-first: triage completes locally; report is created before any network sync.

commitments.text: The client must create a pending report locally upon triage completion, regardless of network state. The report_id must be generated client-side and used as the idempotency key for all subsequent sync operations.
commitments.rationale: Ensures local persistence before any network attempt, superseding b_pet_iface_009.

commitments.text: The local decision tree engine produces a deterministic triage result. The result is stored in the pending report along with the version of the decision tree used (tree_version:string).
commitments.rationale: Triage is performed locally per b_offline_001 and b_offline_004.

commitments.text: POST /sync/upload accepts a JSON body with report_id, triage_data (object), vector_clock (object), and idempotency_key (same as report_id). Returns 200 with sync_status (merged, conflicted) and server_version (object).
commitments.rationale: Async upload per b_sync_001; idempotency prevents duplicate processing.

commitments.text: GET /sync/pull?since=<timestamp> returns a JSON array of reports modified after the given timestamp, each with report_id, triage_data, vector_clock, and status. Supports pagination via next_token.
commitments.rationale: Allows client to pull updates from the clinic backend, supporting multi-clinic replication.

commitments.text: Network failure during sync upload or pull must not be terminal. The sync queue must retain the report with status pending; the retry ledger records the attempt and schedules a retry.
commitments.rationale: Offline-first: network failure is recoverable, superseding b_pet_iface_005.

commitments.text: The sync queue processes pending reports in FIFO order. Each sync attempt records timestamp, HTTP status, error code, and retry count in the retry ledger. After a configurable max retries, the report transitions to failed_terminal.

When a sync upload detects a vector clock conflict, the response includes conflict_payload with local_version (object), server_version (object), and conflicting_fields (array of field names). The client must display a conflict resolution screen.
commitments.rationale: Conflict detection per b_conflict_001 and b_conflict_003.

commitments.text: Clinical fields (diagnosis, vet edits, case status) must use vector clock conflict detection. Low-risk derived metadata (UI cursors, cache timestamps) use last-writer-wins.
The system must never auto-resolve conflicts on clinical fields. All such conflicts require explicit clinician resolution via the conflict resolution screen.

After clinician resolution, the client sends POST /sync/resolve with report_id, chosen_version (object), and updated vector_clock. The server applies the chosen version and returns 200 with merged status.

Each pending report transitions through states: pending -> queued -> syncing -> merged (success) or conflicted (conflict detected) or failed_retryable (network error) or failed_terminal (max retries exceeded). Conflicted reports transition to requires_review after clinician resolution.
commitments.rationale: Defines lifecycle per b_pending_004 and b_sync_004.

commitments.text: Pending reports must survive app restart and process kill. The local store uses SQLite with write-ahead logging.
The local pending report store must not be treated as an authoritative diagnosis source for clinical decisions. It is a transient sync buffer.

Every report payload includes a vector_clock object mapping clinic_id to version number. The server increments its own version on each accepted update. The client maintains the vector clock locally and sends it with every sync upload.
commitments.rationale: Vector clock per b_conflict_001 for conflict detection.

commitments.text: Low-risk metadata fields (UI cursors, cache timestamps) use last-writer-wins. The server and client must mark these fields in the schema as LWW, and the conflict resolution logic must not promote them to vector clock fields.

The client must never silently overwrite cloud-side veterinary modifications. When a sync pull returns a report with a higher vector clock version for the clinic, the client must update its local copy and flag any local pending changes for conflict review.
